title: Multi-Store Autobiographical Trajectory Mining with Proactor-Safe Read-Only Handshake
author: Antigravity Book-to-Skill Forge (book-to-skill-forge)
context: Autonomous coding agent sessions produce rich, high-volume execution histories across two decoupled stores: an append-only JSONL event stream in brain/<cid>/transcript.jsonl and a relational SQLite database in conversations/<cid>.db. Concurrently, IDE worker proactors maintain live WAL locks on active session databases. Mining these multi-gigabyte corpora for architectural friction, error clusters, and proven invariants risks lock starvation, file corruption, and memory exhaustion if opened in default read-write mode or scanned via full-corpus string iteration.
distilled_learning: Autobiographical trajectory mining must enforce three non-negotiable architectural invariants: (1) Proactor-Safe Read-Only Handshake via SQLite URI mode ('file:<path>?mode=ro', Rule 22) to prevent lock contention with active IDE worker processes; (2) Binary Byte-Offset Seek Tables scanned once in binary mode ('rb') to map step indices to byte ranges, enabling O(1) random retrieval across multi-megabyte JSONL streams without loading entire files into memory (Rule 48); and (3) Relational Fallback to conversations/<cid>.db when brain/<cid>/ artifact directories encounter IDE system protection boundaries or permission restrictions (Rule 46).

claims.assertion: Connecting to active SQLite WAL databases using URI read-only mode ('file:<path>?mode=ro') prevents proactor lock contention and eliminates database corruption risks during concurrent session execution.
Binary byte-offset lookup tables compiled once in binary mode enable O(1) seek extraction of execution steps across gigabyte-scale logs without full-file memory allocation.

When IDE system protection boundaries restrict direct file reads from brain/<cid>/ artifact stores, the relational conversations/<cid>.db steps table provides complete, decoupled trajectory introspection without halting.
